paragraphs: Rav Zevid bar Oshaya, chapter Hasokher, in Amemar’s time. It is true that this is the reading in Yevamot 96a and Avodah Zarah 33,beginning of side b. It appears a scribal error in the Gemara: Avodah Zarah 6b says Rav Zevid recited bidve Rabbi Oshaya; Rashi explains, in Rabbi Oshaya’s baraita, which he arranged. There, 56a, bidve Rabbi Oshaya; Rashi likewise explains, in Rabbi Oshaya’s school baraita. This matter in Bava Metzia 92b has bidve Rabbi Oshaya. Bava Batra 95 has “Rav Zevid recited deve Rabbi Oshaya”; Rif and Asheri have bar Oshaya, which too should read bidve Rabbi Oshaya. Shevuot chapter 7, 47a: “Rav Zevid bar Oshaya likewise recited”—it seems to me this too is a scribal error for bidve Rabbi Oshaya—“some say: Rav Zevid recited, Rabbi Oshaya said.” Your eyes see that Rav Zevid was not Rabbi Oshaya’s son. Certainly Yuchasin cites chapter Hasokher, and there bidve Rabbi Oshaya is explicit. As for the statement that he was in Amemar’s time, you will find this only of unqualified Rav Zevid, who was in Amemar’s time as above. Certainly in none of the aforementioned places will you find the understanding that Rav Zevid is bar Oshaya; how could you not find him saying in the name of an Amora or some Tanna? Certainly he did not say in Amemar’s name. It is plain that this is the aforementioned unqualified Rav Zevid, who reported several Amoraim and also Rabbi Oshaya’s baraita. Understand this. Rav Zevid of Nehardea too was in Amemar’s time, and is not the unqualified Rav Zevid.
